idiom_name: companion-object factory methods plus case-class defaults
implementation_notes: Scala case classes give construction, copy and structural equality for free: Customer(name = "Ada", tier = Tier.Vip) with default parameter values is the baseline fixture, and base.copy(tier = Tier.Trial) covers variation - so a dedicated mother is needed only for multi-object graphs or named business scenarios, usually as methods on the Customer companion object or on a TestData singleton in src/test/scala. ScalaTest/Specs2/MUnit supply the wiring, and ScalaCheck Arbitrary generators replace the mother when randomized data is the point. Prefer companion-object factories for canonical domain examples and case-class defaults/copy for everything else.
pitfalls: Case-class copy is shallow: nested collections (addresses: List[Address]) or mutable members are shared with the original instance, so a test that mutates them corrupts the fixture.
Default parameter values on the production case class blur intended values and fallbacks; put test-specific defaults in the mother, not the domain type.
A global object TestData holding mutable state (counters, mutable maps) is a singleton shared across parallel test suites.
ScalaCheck/Arbitrary generators produce type-valid but unconstrained data; without explicit Gen constraints they hand tests the same domain-invalid states a careless mother would.
